question:
Read the below statements marked as Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Mark the correct option:

Assertion (A): PSLV is known as ISRO’s workhorse vehicle.

Reason (R): It can launch satellites of multiple sizes into various orbits with consistent success.

options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A): PSLV is known as ISRO’s workhorse vehicle.**

 
 
• The **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** is one of the most reliable and versatile launch vehicles developed by the **Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO).**
 
• PSLV has earned the title of the "workhorse" due to its consistent performance in launching satellites for domestic and international purposes. ***Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Reason (R): It can launch satellites of multiple sizes into various orbits with consistent success.**
 
 
• PSLV has the capability to launch **small, medium, and large satellites** into various orbits, including **geostationary orbit, polar orbit, and sun-synchronous orbit.**
 
• It has demonstrated **consistent success** by completing more than **50 missions** with minimal failures. This includes launching satellites for purposes like remote sensing, navigation, and scientific research. ***Hence, Reason (R) is correct.***
 
• Reason (R) explains the Assertion because the versatility and reliability of PSLV are the key reasons why it is considered ISRO’s workhorse vehicle. ***Hence, the correct answer is: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **PSLV Overview:**

 
 
• The **Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle (PSLV)** was developed by **ISRO** in the early 1990s and achieved its first successful launch in **October 1994.**
 
• It has different configurations such as **PSLV-C** (Core), **PSLV-XL** (Extended), and **PSLV-DL** (Dual Strap-On), allowing flexibility in payload capacity.
 
• PSLV is capable of placing **satellites weighing up to 1,750 kg** into sun-synchronous orbits and lighter satellites into higher altitudes.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of PSLV:**
 
 
• PSLV has launched over **350 satellites** for various countries, making India a preferred destination for satellite launches.
 
• In **February 2017, PSLV-C37** set a world record by successfully deploying **104 satellites in a single mission.**
 
• It has been used for notable missions like **Mangalyaan (Mars Orbiter Mission)** and the **Chandrayaan-1 lunar mission.**
 
 
 
• **Key Features and Applications:**
 
 
• **Versatility:** PSLV can launch satellites into different types of orbits, including **geostationary transfer orbits (GTO)**, sun-synchronous polar orbits, and low Earth orbits.
 
• **Cost-Effective:** PSLV offers economical launches compared to other international launch vehicles, making it attractive for global customers.
 
• **Scientific and Commercial Applications:** PSLV is used for earth observation, navigation, communication, and interplanetary missions.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **ISRO’s Launch Vehicles:**

 
 
• **PSLV:** Known for its reliability and versatility, widely used for launching satellites into low Earth orbit and polar orbits.
 
• **GSLV:** The Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle is used for launching heavier satellites into geostationary orbit.
 
• **SSLV:** The Small Satellite Launch Vehicle is designed to cater to the increasing demand for small satellite launches.
 
 
 
• **Global Comparisons:**
 
 
• **SpaceX Falcon 9:** Known for reusability and launching heavy payloads.
 
• **Ariane 5:** Used by the European Space Agency for launching heavy payloads into geostationary orbit.
